passages.notes: UTF-8 body SHA256 including final LF 97ad4723bc068a2356abf4bd4c55d7567a6690ee1266d2cef3537ca433298a0a. Target conclusion: Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate. Historical conclusion: Per Dominum. Every complete petition word agrees. Pustet omits the target comma after ut and inserts a comma after Vincentii. Both independently read pages print Adesto, Domine,; the 1962 has no XI between supplicationibus and nostris. The historical saint-day prayer actually stops at Per Dominum.; its cue is not expanded as if printed. The independently read complete Praesta prayer at PustetPDF390/printed304 witnesses every word in the target longer conclusion contiguously through in unitate. The target actual stop at in unitate is retained, without importing the formula subsequent ejusdem Spiritus sancti Deus. Calendar Jesum represents the target printed Iesum under the established consonantal-i convention.

work.description: A project-created editorial source projection containing bounded Latin prayer bodies in date-specific artifacts. It is neither an edition of a historical hand missal nor an edition of the Missale Romanum. Each artifact records the transformation rule over separate public-domain antecedent and 1962 page-image witnesses; its passages let consumers cite the projected bodies without assigning Triptych's target-controlled collation choices to the antecedent printing.
